title: In Gabriel's Hand a Mighty Stone
description: In Gabriel's Hand a Mighty Stone in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 59, headed “Babylon fallen, Rev. 18. 20 21”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In Gab-riel's hand a might-y stone Lies, a fair type of Ba-by-lon ''Pro-phets, re-joice, and, all ye saints, "God shall a-venge your long com-plaints."

lines: In Gabriel's hand a mighty stone
Lies, a fair type of Babylon
He said, and dreadful as he stood,
He sunk the milstone in the flood:
"Thus, and no more be found at all."

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
